newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dairy group details planned Te Rapa development.
newsitem.headline: NZ dairy group details planned Te Rapa development.

text.p: The New Zealand Dairy Group on Thursday said it had begun planning for potential development of its Te Rapa site, including a possible joint venture with companies in the energy sector for a substantial co-generation power plant.

NZDG said that as part of the company's long-term planning it would soon approach the Waikato District Council and Environment Waikato to begin the resource management process for: a new cream processing facility to be ready by the flush of 1997; a new milk powder plant to be ready by the flush of 1998; and an electricity co-generation plant, through a joint venture
NZDG said it was planning to present proposals to a consent hearing early next year.

"The proposed developments have the potential to produce significant long-term benefits for shareholders by offering the group low-cost energy and substantially increased capacity", NZDG chairman John Storey said in a statement.
The proposed co-generation plant would not only provide electricity and steam to Te Rapa but offer electricity across the group and provide power for Waikato and national needs.
Earlier, the New Zealand Press Association reported that a number of major players in the electricity and gas industry were jostling for selection as NZDG's co-generation partner.
They were said to include Mercury Energy, Natural Gas Corporation, Contact Energy and Waikato supplier WEL Energy.

"A window of opportunity exists to build a co-generation plant, using new aeronautically derived gas turbine technology. This would help counter New Zealand's anticipated electricity generation short-fall and also, as a by-product, produce steam for use in the adjacent dairy factories," Storey said.

"Energy is our second highest cost after labour, so a scheme such as this has the potential to contribute greatly to our objective of becoming the world's lowest-cost producer of high quality dairy products."

Storey said the combined projects would have a "major beneficial effect" on the regional economy. A Dairy Group spokesman said it was too early to speculate on the partner for the co-generation plant as calls for submissions had only just gone out. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
